remarks.para: Irrespective of the number of counts, the Minimum time between syncs must be more than 290 microseconds.

If the time encroaches on that 290us the encoder will halt the collection and return a Framing Error, setting an error value which must be read with UpdateStatus() on the EIM before further readings or commands can be executed on then EIM.
To work out the minimum value that could be set you should start by working out the RPM, Identifying the number of Counts per revolution.
CountsPerSecond = (RPM /60) * CountsPerRev
Min = (CountsPerSecond/1000000) * 290
For Example with an encoder turning at 30RPM With 10000 Counts per revolution the calculation would be:
Min = (5000/1000000) * 290 = 1.45, therefor we round to 2

It should be noted that it is advisable to set a count value of at least 2, and to take into account the coarseness of the movements of stepper motors - if one move on a stepper motor moves accross 3 or 4 counts on the encoder over that Distance it would be travelling at significantly more than the measured RPM.

This sets the action to perform when the reference mark is triggered on the EIM.

remarks.para: It can be set to: not trigger at all, trigger once or trigger continuously.
The options are listed in the enum
Note: when the module is used as an External Master, either in Dynamic Master or Buffered Master collections; The RefAction state is cleared to None

summary.para: tx Sample - Counts per Sample command in buffered master
This is only applicable in buffered master operation
This identifies the number of counts after which each sample pulse should be triggered
tx Sync - Counts per sync pulse as dynamic master
This is only applicable in dynamic master operation
This identifies the number of counts after which each sync pulse should be triggered

remarks.para: Irrespective of the number of counts, the Minimum time between syncs must be more than 290 microseconds.

If the time encroaches on that 290us the encoder will halt the collection and return a Framing Error, setting an error value which must be read with UpdateStatus() on the EIM before further readings or commands can be executed on then EIM.
To work out the minimum value that could be set you should start by working out the RPM, Identifying the number of Counts per revolution.
CountsPerSecond = (RPM /60) * CountsPerRev
Min = (CountsPerSecond/1000000) * 290
For Example with an encoder turning at 30RPM With 10000 Counts per revolution the calculation would be:
Min = (5000/1000000) * 290 = 1.45, therefor we round to 2

It should be noted that it is advisable to set a count value of at least 2, and to take into account the coarseness of the movements of stepper motors - if one move on a stepper motor moves accross 3 or 4 counts on the encoder over that Distance it would be travelling at significantly more than the measured RPM.
